rejected.title: Medicare
card: Medicare is Australia's public health insurance scheme. It is run by the Australian Government and is open to eligible residents.
It is funded mainly from general taxes, including the Medicare levy, which is a small part of a person's taxable income.
Medicare covers or subsidises the cost of many services, such as visits to doctors, tests like blood tests and X-rays, and care as a public patient in a public hospital.
A subsidy means Medicare pays some or all of the fee. A patient may still pay a gap if the provider charges more than the Medicare amount.
rejected.remember: Medicare is tax-funded public insurance that helps pay for doctors, tests and public hospital care.

a.q: Which statement best describes how Medicare is paid for?
opts: Mostly from taxes, including the Medicare levy
Mostly from fees paid each time someone sees a doctor
Mostly from premiums paid to private companies
Mostly from donations given to public hospitals
a.why: Medicare is funded mainly from taxes, and the Medicare levy is part of that. Premiums go to private health insurers, which is a different scheme, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what people pay through their income.

b.q: Tom has a blood test ordered by his GP in Bendigo. The provider charges more than the Medicare amount. What is true about this case?
opts: Medicare pays its part and Tom may pay the gap
Medicare pays nothing because the fee is too high
Medicare pays the full fee, however high it is
Medicare pays only if Tom has private insurance
b.why: Medicare subsidises tests, so it pays its set amount. If the provider charges more, Tom may pay the gap. Medicare does not pay any fee in full, and it does not depend on private insurance.
b.clue: A subsidy pays some of the fee, not always all of it.

version.title: Medicare
card: Medicare is Australia's public health insurance scheme. It is run by the Australian Government and is open to citizens, permanent residents and some others.
It is funded from taxes, including the Medicare levy, a small extra charge on most taxpayers' taxable income.
Medicare covers or subsidises many services: visits to doctors, tests such as blood tests and X-rays, and free care as a public patient in a public hospital.
For a doctor's visit or test, Medicare pays a set benefit. If the doctor bulk bills, that benefit is the whole payment. If the doctor charges more, the patient pays the gap.
version.remember: Medicare is tax-funded public insurance that helps pay for doctors, tests and public hospital care.

a.q: Where does most of the money for Medicare come from?
opts: Taxes, including a levy on income
Fees patients pay at each doctor visit
Premiums paid to private health funds
Donations made to public hospitals
a.why: Medicare is funded from taxes, and the Medicare levy on taxable income is part of that. Premiums go to private health insurers, which is a separate scheme.
a.clue: Think about what people pay through the tax system.

b.q: Nadia's GP in Shepparton charges more than the Medicare benefit for her visit. What happens with the cost?
opts: Medicare pays its benefit and Nadia pays the gap
Medicare pays nothing because the fee is higher
Medicare pays the whole fee, however high it is
Medicare pays only if Nadia has private cover
b.why: Medicare pays its set benefit towards the visit, and Nadia pays the rest, called the gap. Medicare's benefit would be the whole payment only if the GP bulk billed. It does not depend on private cover.
b.clue: The benefit is a set amount, whatever the doctor charges.

a.best: Taxes, including a levy on income

b.best: Medicare pays its benefit and Nadia pays the gap
